005package org.wpilib.smartdashboard;
006
007import static org.wpilib.units.Units.Meters;
008
009import java.util.ArrayList;
010import java.util.List;
011import org.wpilib.math.geometry.Pose2d;
012import org.wpilib.math.geometry.Rotation2d;
013import org.wpilib.telemetry.TelemetryLoggable;
014import org.wpilib.telemetry.TelemetryTable;
015import org.wpilib.tunable.ComplexTunable;
016import org.wpilib.tunable.TunableRegistry;
017import org.wpilib.tunable.TunableTable;
018import org.wpilib.units.measure.Distance;
019
020/**
021 * 2D representation of game field for dashboards.
022 *
023 * <p>An object's pose is the location shown on the dashboard view. Note that for the robot, this
024 * may or may not match the internal odometry. For example, the robot is shown at a particular
025 * starting location, the pose in this class would represent the actual location on the field, but
026 * the robot's internal state might have a 0,0,0 pose (unless it's initialized to something
027 * different).
028 *
029 * <p>As the user is able to edit the pose, code performing updates should get the robot pose,
030 * transform it as appropriate (e.g. based on wheel odometry), and set the new pose.
031 *
032 * <p>This class provides methods to set the robot pose, but other objects can also be shown by
033 * using the getObject() function. Other objects can also have multiple poses (which will show the
034 * object at multiple locations).
035 */
036public class Field2d implements TelemetryLoggable, ComplexTunable, AutoCloseable {
037  /** Constructor. */
038  public Field2d() {
039    m_objects.add(new FieldObject2d("Robot", Pose2d.ZERO));
040  }
041
042  @Override
043  public synchronized void close() {
044    TunableRegistry.remove(this);
045  }
046
047  /**
048   * Set the robot pose from a Pose object.
049   *
050   * @param pose 2D pose
051   */
052  public synchronized void setRobotPose(Pose2d pose) {
053    m_objects.get(0).setPose(pose);
054  }
055
056  /**
057   * Set the robot pose from x, y, and rotation.
058   *
059   * @param x X location, in meters
060   * @param y Y location, in meters
061   * @param rotation rotation
062   */
063  public synchronized void setRobotPose(double x, double y, Rotation2d rotation) {
064    m_objects.get(0).setPose(x, y, rotation);
065  }
066
067  /**
068   * Set the robot pose from x, y, and rotation.
069   *
070   * @param x X location
071   * @param y Y location
072   * @param rotation rotation
073   */
074  public synchronized void setRobotPose(Distance x, Distance y, Rotation2d rotation) {
075    m_objects.get(0).setPose(x.in(Meters), y.in(Meters), rotation);
076  }
077
078  /**
079   * Get the robot pose.
080   *
081   * @return 2D pose
082   */
083  public synchronized Pose2d getRobotPose() {
084    return m_objects.get(0).getPose();
085  }
086
087  /**
088   * Get or create a field object.
089   *
090   * @param name The field object's name.
091   * @return Field object
092   */
093  public synchronized FieldObject2d getObject(String name) {
094    for (FieldObject2d obj : m_objects) {
095      if (obj.m_name.equals(name)) {
096        return obj;
097      }
098    }
099    FieldObject2d obj = new FieldObject2d(name);
100    m_objects.add(obj);
101    publishChildTunable(obj.m_name, obj.m_posesTunable);
102    return obj;
103  }
104
105  /**
106   * Get the robot object.
107   *
108   * @return Field object for robot
109   */
110  public synchronized FieldObject2d getRobotObject() {
111    return m_objects.get(0);
112  }
113
114  @Override
115  public void logTo(TelemetryTable table) {
116    synchronized (this) {
117      for (FieldObject2d obj : m_objects) {
118        synchronized (obj) {
119          table.log(obj.m_name, obj.m_poses.toArray(new Pose2d[0]));
120        }
121      }
122    }
123  }
124
125  @Override
126  public String getTelemetryType() {
127    return "Field2d";
128  }
129
130  /**
131   * Gets the tunable type.
132   *
133   * @return Field2d type.
134   */
135  @Override
136  public String getTunableType() {
137    return "Field2d";
138  }
139
140  /**
141   * Publishes field objects to a tunable table.
142   *
143   * @param table Tunable table.
144   */
145  @Override
146  public synchronized void publishTunable(TunableTable table) {
147    for (FieldObject2d obj : m_objects) {
148      table.publish(obj.m_name, obj.m_posesTunable);
149    }
150  }
151
152  private final List<FieldObject2d> m_objects = new ArrayList<>();
153}
